prompt:
Use case: identity-preserve. Production animation extension of an ADOPTED pixel game character, not a redesign. The attached sheet is the approved design and poses at nearest 4x; use its first standing pose as exact identity, palette, scale and proportions. Same adopted brown/cream tiny hedgehog with clearly sharp quills, pointed snout, small dark eye and very short feet. Keep normal idle body size ~18 native pixels; enhanced defense spikes already adopted and will be reused. Do NOT inflate its body or turn into a round cute toy.
Create only these NEW motion poses: 3 columns x 2 rows, six isolated poses facing RIGHT. Four genuinely distinct tiny scuttling WALK phases with alternating near/far front and rear paws: reach, gather, opposite reach, opposite gather. Keep head and normal quill silhouette stable and sharp, small feet visible. Last two: (4) small alive flinch with feet braced and face withdrawing slightly, (5) recovering to normal stance. Do NOT regenerate defense spike/ball poses. No dust, glow, shadows or letters.
Transparent RGBA background, equal grid cells, generous transparent gutters, consistent full-body scale and ground baseline, complete feet and limbs. Clean chunky square pixel clusters for a small game sprite enlarged into the output, same muted palette, 1-pixel native dark brown contour, upper-left illumination. No smooth airbrushed illustration, no labels/grid/text/background/ground shadows/additional people. Same head and face in every cell. Meaningful limb changes, never just translated duplicates. Output only the motion sheet.
